title: Cranberry Sauce

drivers.name: Store closed Monday for renovation
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; historical data shows ~20% of weekly sales occur on Monday (based on 13-week average). No other drivers present. No prior closure effect to adjust for.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 9.1. Store closure on Monday (no sales) reduces expected volume. No promotion, but price increased 2.1% above regular. Past promotions show noisy uplifts; noise-adjusted estimate is x1.0. The week after a promotion typically sees x0.68 demand, but no prior promotion in this week's window. The only driver is the store closure, which likely removes ~20% of the week's sales (Monday). The price increase has a negligible effect given historical noise. No event or seasonal driver. The classical model’s x1.0 is reasonable given no strong evidence. Adjust only for closure.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 9.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 19.7 | 10%-90%: 2.1 - 17.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-81% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
